messages:
jordan: paging — sudden spike in 5xx from inference-gateway (us-west-2) starting ~09:11 PDT. Dashboard shows 503/502 and timeouts. incident-bot alerted. Can oncall triage?

ops-bot: Incident created: P1 - inference-gateway 5xx spike (4360001234). Pager duty notified.

maria: seeing client error reports, a handful of customers hit increased latency and failures. Not widespread yet but growing.

leo: grabbing logs from the gateway now. quick check: envoy upstream_retries are through the roof. looks like retry loop + some upstreams returning 502 then circuit-breakers trip.

leo: log snippet: ```
[09:12:11] upstream/cluster: "model-shard-7" - 502 Bad Gateway
[09:12:12] envoy retrying request to model-shard-7 (attempt 2)
[09:12:13] circuit_breaker: ejections=3, consecutive 5xx=8
```

sam (oncall): I'm on it. tagging infra and runtime. quick question — are we actively rolling any LB/route config?

jordan: not that I know of, no config rollouts in last 24h. however we did enable a new retry shadow policy for small experiment yesterday. could be interaction.

anna: I'm seeing route-weight skew for /v1/generate traffic — most routed to shard pool A (model-shard-7/8) due to sticky policy. If those shards have transient latency, retries amplify.

sam (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) disable gateway retries globally for now 2) reduce route weight to shift traffic off shard-7 3) increase CB thresholds temporarily to avoid aggressive ejection 4) notify customers about degraded availability. Who can apply changes?

leo: I can push the retry toggle fast. patch: ```sh
# disable gateway-level retries
kubectl -n infra patch configmap envoy-gateway --type merge -p '{"data":{"retry.enabled":"false"}}'
```

deploy-bot: Deploy job queued: apply-configmap-envoy-gateway (job 7821). ETA ~30s.

leo: pushed. confirm: envoy retry counters dropping?

anna: counters show retry attempts down 90% within 20s. latency still elevated on model-shard-7 though.

sam (oncall): next, shift weights. anna, can you cut weight to shard-7 to 0.1 and distribute to shard-3/4?

anna: doing a soft weight shift. command: ```sh
# adjust route weights in LB control plane
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' 
  https://lb-control.us-west-2/api/route-weight 
  -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","weights":{"shard-3":0.45,"shard-4":0.45,"shard-7":0.1}}'
```

ops-bot: Route config change applied (request id 0f3a2c).

leo: verifying: traffic distribution showing ~45/45/10 now. backend error rate for shard-7 dropping as traffic shifts. overall 5xx trending down.

maria: started drafting a short customer notice. will post on status.redwood shortly.

sam (oncall): CB thresholds — we need to avoid permanent ejections while we mitigate. anna, can you bump the circuit breaker max_retries and ejection window on shard-7 only for 15m?

anna: yes. patching cluster config: ```yaml
clusters:
  - name: model-shard-7
    circuit_breakers:
      thresholds:
        - priority: DEFAULT
          max_retries: 10
          interval: 60s
          base_ejection_time: 30s
```

deploy-bot: Config update rolled to envoy proxies in us-west-2 (rollout id c9d4).

leo: ejections reduced, request failures smoothing out. average latency back to baseline for shard-3/4, shard-7 still slightly higher but healthy.

jordan: quick root-cause hypothesis: retry amplification created a retry storm towards a subset of shards that were already experiencing transient latency, triggering CB ejections and causing wider 5xx.

sam (oncall): agree. immediate mitigations done. next steps: 1) keep retries disabled for 30m 2) run deeper analysis on why shard-7 latency rose (hardware, GC, network) 3) prepare post-incident RCA if customer impact continues 4) oncall handoff protocol — I'll own until 10:00 PDT then hand to leo.

maria: status page update posted: "We are investigating increased 5xx rates affecting text generation in US‑West. Mitigations applied; some customers may experience intermittent failures. We'll post updates."

leo: doing heap/cpu checks on model servers behind shard-7. early signal: CPU spikes coincident with high queue depth. attaching quick perf stats: ```
shard-7 cpu: 92%  - high GC pause event at 09:10
shard-3 cpu: 45%
queue depth shard-7: 120 (norm 30)
```

anna: could be a model hot shard due to sticky routing + fanout. we should consider prefix caching or more even hashing for routing in the long term.

sam (oncall): agree. create a ticket for routing policy review and add stress tests that simulate sticky hot shards.

jordan: any customer escalations?

maria: two enterprise customers opened support tickets reporting failures in the 09:11–09:18 window. CS is handling and will mirror this thread.

sam (oncall): I'll keep monitoring for 30m. handoff to leo at 10:00 if stable. please add any ops notes to the incident doc. tag me if error rate goes above 2% again.

ops-bot: Incident updated: Mitigations applied (retries disabled, route weights adjusted, CB thresholds relaxed). Current severity: P2 (4360001450).

leo: confirming metrics: 5xx rate from 6.8% -> 0.9% over 10 minutes. latency median restored.

jordan: thanks team. postmortem action items: 
- investigate GC/CPU on shard-7 nodes (owner: leo)
- evaluate retry/shadow policies interactions (owner: jane-research)
- routing policy change to avoid sticky concentration (owner: anna)
- add circuit-breaker tuning runbook (owner: sam)

maria: I'll schedule a customer follow-up for the affected accounts and link incident doc.

sam (oncall): handing off to leo in 45m unless anything regresses. good work. :thumbsup:
